name: Raku firing
summary: A short, hot firing of one small piece. The potter opens the kiln and pulls the glowing piece out with tongs.
how: Bisque fire the hand-built piece to about 800 °C.
Dip it in a lead glaze.
Fire it alone in a small kiln until the glaze melts, at 800 to 1000 °C.
Pull it out with tongs and let it cool in the air.

origin.note: Chōjirō fires hand-built bowls one at a time for Sen no Rikyū and pulls them from the hot kiln.

adoptions.via: The Raku workshop fires each tea bowl alone and pulls it hot from the kiln.
